lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.unitTitle: PF3 — Budgeting and Saving: Running the Adult Budget
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: operating a budget month over month

focus: operating a budget month over month
objective: Operate a fictional budget across three months, accumulate the variance the variable categories produce, and report the surplus that actually exists rather than the one that was planned.
scenario: The budget and the three months of spending below belong to a fictional adult. Every figure is invented for this exercise.
safetyNotes: Every figure, person, employer, institution, offer, account, and document on this task sheet is fictional and exists only for practice.
No real transaction is part of this lesson, and no real bank, card, brokerage, tax, or login detail is ever requested. If a task sheet ever appears to ask for one, stop and tell a trusted adult.
This lesson teaches general financial concepts and does not advise anyone about their own money. For a real decision, talk with a trusted adult or a qualified licensed professional.
materials: the fictional budget and monthly totals in these directions

tasks.directions: The fictional adult takes home $3,240 a month. The fixed commitments are rent $1,180, utilities $165, insurance $142, phone $58, and transport $210. The plan allows $480 for food, $120 for household, and $200 for personal spending, and sets aside $350 for savings. Across the first three months the variable categories actually came to $862, $774, and $918.

prompts.text: What do the fixed commitments come to each month?
What does the plan allocate in total each month, savings included?
What monthly surplus does the plan expect?

tasks.directions: Now run the plan forward against what actually happened over the 3 months.

prompts.text: What did the variable categories actually cost across the three months?
What did the plan allow for those categories over the same three months?
What is the cumulative variance after three months?
What surplus has actually accumulated across the three months?

The plan expected $1,005.00 of surplus after three months and produced $851.00. Say whether these three months show a plan that is set too low or a run of ordinary variation, explain what in the figures supports your reading, and state what you would need to see to be more certain.

remediation: If the accumulated surplus comes out at $1,005.00, the variance has not been carried into it. The plan produces $335.00 a month only if the variable categories land on $800.00; they came to $2,554.00 rather than $2,400.00 over the three months, so $154.00 of the expected surplus has already been spent.
extension: Rewrite the variable allowance so that it would have covered all three months as they actually happened, and say what has to be reduced elsewhere to keep the same $350 of savings.
